grades.quote: The atomic exchange instructions on the two processors will both be writing into the cache block containing the spinlock.
grades.reason: Directly identifies competing writes to the same cache block and explains that read-only waiting avoids the resulting coherence traffic.

grades.quote: Most typically, the cache where the writing occurs invalidates all the other caches’ copies so that it has exclusive ownership. If one of the other processors now wants to write, the block needs to be flushed out of the first cache and loaded exclusively into the second. If the two processors keep alternately writing into the same block, there will be continual traffic on the memory interconnect as the cache block is transferred back and forth between the two caches.
grades.reason: Explains both repeated exchange writes and the invalidations and ownership transfers that make contention expensive.

grades.quote: Each iteration swaps one into lk->locked and checks the previous value; if the previous value is zero, then we’ve acquired the lock, and the swap will have set lk->locked to one. If the previous value is one, then some other CPU holds the lock, and the fact that we atomically swapped one into lk->locked didn’t change its value.
grades.reason: Establishes that failed retries repeatedly write the shared lock word, but does not explain cache invalidations or coherence traffic.
Discusses CAS instructions and ABA avoidance, but does not explain cache-coherence traffic from contended atomic-exchange spinlocks.
